title: PH Payroll (payroll system for Philippine companies)
tagline: A web payroll system for Philippine companies, installed once per company on the office network with no internet needed. A team project; my role was developer.
problem: Philippine payroll has to get SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG and withholding tax right, plus the labour department's (DOLE) pay rules for overtime, holidays and night work, and the rates change. One wrong rule means wrong pay.
built: A Django and PostgreSQL application with server-rendered pages and HTMX, installed with Docker Compose. Three roles (Admin, HR/Payroll Officer, Employee) cover employee records, attendance, leave, loans and 13th-month pay. A payroll run is computed, approved and locked; a locked payslip is a saved copy that later rate changes never alter. The pay rules are plain Python with no database code, and money is always a Decimal. The code is proprietary, so the repository is private.
highlights: Government rates are data, not code: each table has a start date and an official source, and an Admin adds the next one when the law changes
Government numbers are encrypted in the database, and an audit log records who changed what, and when
Payslips as PDF, a payroll summary that opens in Excel, and monthly remittance summaries with CSV export
No internet at run time: every page asset ships inside the app, with daily backups and optional HTTPS
testing: pytest unit tests cover every pay rule and every page, and Playwright browser tests click through the app like a person. Both run on GitHub Actions on every push, the unit tests against PostgreSQL. Every feature has a written test case, and a test fails when that document and the code stop agreeing.
